normalization_or_editorial_flags.issue: Normalize sentence-final punctuation consistently; several declarative rows use ASCII periods while Arabic question rows use Arabic question marks.
ربطات حذائك is understandable but 'tie your shoelaces' is more directly أربطة حذائك; review lexical standardization.
Prefer في وقت فراغك over بوقت فراغك for standard MSA.
Normalize comma/quotation typography to a single Arabic/Unicode house style.
إلى كم ساعة من النوم تحتاج؟ is awkward; prefer كم ساعة من النوم تحتاج؟.
ماذا ستقومين بتسمية طفلك؟ is grammatical but heavy; ماذا ستسمين طفلك؟ is more natural MSA.
Arabic definite الحفلة means 'the party'; English says 'this party'. Tighten deixis if exact standalone equivalence is required.
Remove stray space before question mark.
غاضب على is less standard than غاضب من/بسبب for the target MSA register.
Tag question is a literal هل فعلت؟; a polished MSA learner pair may prefer أليس كذلك؟ depending on intended nuance.
يا شباب is colloquial/register-specific against a nominal MSA target; review whether to retain.
Normalize dialogue punctuation and tanwin/spacing; rank 895 also adds 'only' not present in English.
صديقك may mean friend and does not unambiguously encode boyfriend; use clearer relationship wording if specificity is required.
Arabic says 'the washing machine'; English says 'this washing machine'. Tighten deixis if needed.
English includes 'please' absent from Arabic; align politeness marker.
Arabic literally asks 'Who gave you the right...?' while English asks 'What gives you the right...?'; idiomatically close but not literal.
